## What changed

**A deferred PostgreSQL barrier no longer demands `--force`.** The finding says
in as many words that the climb can start now — and then the gate refused to
start without a flag that means "ignore the warnings". A person resolves that
contradiction the only way available: by learning to type `--force`, which also
silences everything else, including whatever appears on the next `resume`.

It is safe to let the climb begin because the barrier is enforced where it
actually matters: `run` checks the requirement before every step and stops on
its own in front of the one it cannot satisfy — before taking that step's
backup. A barrier on the *first* step is still critical, and `--force` does not
clear it. Other warnings are unchanged: an active `apt-daily.timer` still needs
a deliberate `--force`, because nothing else will stop it from taking the dpkg
lock halfway through an install.

This is the same reasoning that already exempts the OS ceiling, which has its
own `--allow-unsupported-os`: a scheduled task is not a defect to wave through.
